clue.text: Sauce like this always served up

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word for always is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A diner insists a particular sauce must always come with the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SO plus AY written upwards (YA).
explanation.definitionFit: Soy sauce is called soya sauce in Britain, so soya on its own names the condiment.

clue.text: Fast speed over endlessly polluted air in a show of swagger

parts.note: Mach I (Mach one) is the speed of sound, a fast speed

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: smog is polluted air

explanation.surface: A fast car tears through smoggy air, its driver showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: MACH I is Mach one, the speed of sound; SMOG without its end gives SMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive masculine pride, a swaggering display of toughness.

clue.text: Face having to use an old phone?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the face of a clock or watch
second meaning: to ... a number on a rotary telephone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second sense: modern phones are tapped, older ones had a rotary dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock face is its dial, and placing a call on a rotary telephone was called dialling.

clue.text: Chubby lad's bottom almost all visible in cast off

parts.note: a putto is a chubby cherub boy in Renaissance art

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a seat is a bottom, the part one sits on

explanation.surface: A cherub in a painting shows nearly all of his bare behind.
explanation.walkthrough: PUTTO plus SEAT without its last letter (SEA); 'all visible in' just carries the picture of the painted cherub.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off is to untie a boat and set out, which is what putting to sea means for a ship.

clue.text: Country recipe with a so-called fish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, seen on prescriptions
the film A Fish Called Wanda names a fish called Wanda

explanation.surface: A national dish is made from a fish known by some odd name.
explanation.walkthrough: A Fish Called Wanda is a 1988 comedy film, so the fish so called is WANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked nation in central Africa.

clue.text: Use mouse to follow movement that keeps players together

parts.note: to click is to press a computer mouse button
to track is to follow

explanation.surface: Someone uses a computer mouse to follow a moving thing on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A click track is a recorded metronome beat that musicians hear in headphones so they stay in time.

clue.text: Very funny sex with a Dolores

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is text-speak for something very funny
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a hilarious bedroom encounter with a woman called Dolores.
explanation.walkthrough: In Nabokov's novel, Lolita is the pet name of Dolores Haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the nickname Humbert gives the girl Dolores Haze in Nabokov's novel.

clue.text: Widow may have one quick look when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says the word for a quick look is matched by its sound, not spelling; the run of letters inside speaking is a coincidence

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A grieving widow may sneak a glance at something.
explanation.walkthrough: A widow's peak is a V-shaped point of hair on the forehead, so the widow in the clue is not bereaved at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow's peak is a hairline dipping to a point in the middle of the forehead.

clue.text: Arab will be in Italy tomorrow, dropping off daughter

indicators.note: dropping off means the daughter letter is let go from the word

parts.note: domani is the Italian word for tomorrow

explanation.surface: A visitor says he will reach Italy tomorrow after leaving his daughter somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani, from the Gulf sultanate of Oman, is one of the Arab peoples.

clue.text: Poorly, cutting last visit as distasteful

indicators.note: cutting last means the final letter is trimmed away

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill
to come is to visit

explanation.surface: Being ill, someone cuts short a final visit, finding it unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: UNWELL without its last letter (UNWEL) plus COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted or is disagreeable, so it is distasteful.

clue.text: King beginning to attack last rebels in the north

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of attack is taken
in means the reworked letters go inside the following ones
rebels means the letters of last revolt into a new order

explanation.surface: A king leads a final assault against northern insurgents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last rebels' looks like the final rebels; 'last' is the fodder and 'rebels' the verb telling it to rise up, before it is set in 'the north'.
explanation.definitionFit: Athelstan was the tenth-century ruler often called the first monarch of all England.

clue.text: Sound of keys rattling in prison

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the light ringing sound of metal on metal

explanation.surface: A jailer's keys jangle in a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is both a short metallic ringing noise and an informal name for jail.

clue.text: Can't find source of whisky young lady drinks

indicators.note: drinks means the young lady takes the whisky source inside her

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman, here a young lady
Islay is a Scottish island famous for its malt whisky

explanation.surface: A young woman drinking whisky can no longer locate things.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is a Hebridean island whose distilleries make peaty Scotch whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone mislays something they have put it somewhere and cannot find it.

clue.text: Moony features of musical girl I just met

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the dark plains, or seas, on the Moon
second meaning: the West Side Story song begins 'I just met a girl named ...'

explanation.walkthrough: Maria is the plural of mare, a lunar sea; the second half quotes the song from West Side Story.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunar seas are called maria, and Maria is the heroine Tony sings about in West Side Story.

clue.text: Iodine for one upset (not terminally sick) patient

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order
not terminally means the last letter of sick is dropped

explanation.surface: Iodine is applied to a distressed patient who is unwell but not dying.
explanation.walkthrough: SICK loses its end to give SIC; SIC and PATIENT are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is a classic example of a germ-killing agent dabbed on wounds.

clue.text: In fact, two hands should be replaced by another professional

indicators.note: should be replaced by means the two hands are swapped out for the other one

parts.note: actually means in fact
L and L, left twice, two hands
R, right, is the other hand

explanation.surface: Someone notes that two workers ought to be swapped for a different specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for left and R for right, so the two left hands in ACTUALLY give way to a right hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuary is a trained expert who calculates insurance risks and premiums.

clue.text: Don't go to bed, taking in English poet

indicators.note: taking in means the English letter is placed inside

parts.note: to stay up is to not go to bed; in a down clue that is the word stay written upwards

explanation.surface: Someone stays up late reading an English poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't go to bed' is STAY UP, which in a down clue means STAY is written upwards (YATS). 'English poet' tempts, but Yeats was Irish: English is only E.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was a Nobel-winning Irish writer of verse.

clue.text: Bed's base son breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the son letter breaks into the word for base

parts.note: the root is the base of something

explanation.surface: A son smashes the base of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to sleep, their bed for the night.

clue.text: Joiner featured in a Shakespeare play, though not much at the start

indicators.note: not much at the start means the first letter is removed, much being abbreviated M

parts.note: MND is the usual abbreviation for A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A joiner appears in a Shakespeare play, though barely in the opening scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: Snug the joiner is one of the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'and' is a conjunction, a word linking clauses.

clue.text: Gone astray, I have picked up old clothes

indicators.note: clothes means the word for old wraps around the other piece

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: I've is a contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone who has wandered off has gathered some old garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as garments but is a verb: the word for old dresses the reversed contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to depart from a path, so having deviated means having strayed.

clue.text: A for Aristotle

parts.note: Aristotle wrote in Greek, so the clue asks what the Greeks call the character we write as A

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a phonetic spelling (A for Apple), but Aristotle points to Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The first character of the Greek alphabet corresponds to the Roman letter A.

clue.text: Being a sport, send quick message to practise at first on golf

parts.note: to ping someone is to send them a quick message

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of practise is used

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A good sport messages a friend to come and practise golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong is the informal name for table tennis, a game played with bats.

clue.text: Does she have half a case against heartless employer?

definitions.text: Does she have half a case against heartless employer?

parts.note: the accusative is a grammatical case; half its ten letters is the first five

indicators.note: heartless means the whole middle of employer goes, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: A woman wonders whether she has a partial legal claim against a cruel boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The case is grammatical, not legal: ACCUSATIVE halved gives ACCUS, and EMPLOYER without its heart leaves ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who charges another with wrongdoing has a case against them, making her the complainant.

clue.text: Settlement: the last to pay

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is a colon

indicators.note: the last to means only the final letter of pay is taken

explanation.surface: A deal is agreed: the latecomer will cover the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon in the clue is not just punctuation; it supplies its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a group of settlers or the place they establish in a new land.

clue.text: Come back to host a second game, perhaps

indicators.note: to host means the word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to come back with an answer is to reply

explanation.surface: A team returns to stage another match.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match played again, for instance after a drawn cup tie.

clue.text: Pagans adding verse to biblical book

parts.note: I Kings, First Kings, is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Heathens add a verse to a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse raiders who attacked Britain were heathens, not Christians, worshipping Odin and Thor.

clue.text: Growth of college power

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college

explanation.surface: A college's power is expanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyp is a small growth sticking out of a mucous membrane.

clue.text: Bunch adopting affected attitudes?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small bunch of flowers
second meaning: a whimsical adjective for someone who strikes poses, pretentious

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense, as if from 'pose' plus -y.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bouquet; jokingly, someone forever posing could be called posy.

clue.text: Go out of this world, say, in zero visibility

indicators.note: say signals that the words for go and out of this world are matched by their sound

parts.note: go is a coy word for pee, to urinate, and out of this world means super, excellent; together they are said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone talks of dying and leaving this world in a total fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out of this world' looks like dying; it is PEE plus SUPER, said aloud as PEA SOUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a thick yellowish London fog, through which nothing can be seen.

clue.text: Remove section of enormous table

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone wants to take away part of a huge table.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or eject them from a position.

clue.text: Stagger back to the rear as big bird comes over

indicators.note: comes over means the bird sits above the other piece in this down answer

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird

indicators.note: to the rear means the final letter of back is taken

explanation.surface: Someone reels backwards as a huge bird swoops overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to sway unsteadily, much as one staggers on one's feet.

clue.text: Gang of criminals send a city wild

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A mob of crooks causes mayhem in a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime syndicate is an organised group of gangsters working together.

clue.text: Such a screwdriver very attractive? Not quite

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant, attractive

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a screwdriver is truly gorgeous, then hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: The sonic screwdriver is Doctor Who's gadget, in the BBC science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Who's multi-purpose gadget is known as the sonic screwdriver.
